Walker won the Junior race followed home by Len Bishop and with our other men packing well, we managed to beat the home team once again. Southgate very kindly provided our lads with tea and cakes after the run and we hope to entertain them over our own course next season.
Over our five miles course Field finished a good winner in 30 mins. 8 secs., and Archie Bedford ran well to finish a close second with Ches Walker also well up.
In the 1 mile it was our turn to score a “ maximum ” and we actually had the first three men home, with Jack Brown leading Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker in the good time of 4 min. 31.4 secs.
The Club has met with successes in many open meetings and our team of Walker, Sexton, Beaumont and Underwood won the Mile Medley Relay at the Charlotteville meeting on Whit-Monday.

Cope, was not competing, and Ches Walker won a good race from Archie Bedford, with Len Bishop running well for third place. Frank Kemp made a double of it by winning the 220 yards Junior race, beating Dave Marshall, who is the Surrey champion at this distance.
Vernon, therefore, did extremely well to maintain the same lead, and when Ches Walker took over for the fifth stage we were practically certain of victory.
At the half-way mark a small bunch of runners were at the head of the field, but when they came into the finishing field Ches Walker and Len Herbert were battling it out neck-and-neck.

Stone, the holder, was leading, but Ches Walker was close behind and, moreover, was running very easily, and it was obvious that unless Stone could get away from his opponent on the second lap of the country he had had it!

Walker and Bill Lucas both run well, with the former beating Alec Olney for first place, with Bill third. It was only through Bill " pepping " up the pace with a lap to go that the field broke up and this enabled Walker to use his stronger finishing powers to good advantage.

Smith third, and it seems rather rough on " Mac " that with Harry Churcher not competing we have yet another fine walker to step into his shoes and so keep " Mac " in his usual second position in these events.
Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race.

Chas Walker, although suffering from the after-effects of a cold, ran a good first "leg" which was inside the previous lap record time, held by Bill Lucas, but even so could only hand over in second place to Cook, of Hadleigh A.C.

Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th. All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A.
Charlie Walker was well up to start with but then seemed to ease off with the result that at the end of the first short lap we had no one in the first fifty placings.

Bob Taylor was second in the 440 yards and our team of Walker, Barker, Thomas and Bartlett beat the local club in the 1 mile medley relay. In the Junior events we saw Alan Law score a good double by winning the 100 and 220 yards, while Brian Trower was another dual winner in the 440 and 880 with Bor…

Walker, and Ray found one too good for him in Lloyd-Morgan, the Oxford runner, who won in the good time of 4 min. 19 secs. Ray was a close second but Walker could not make the first four home who all scored points.

Walker brought us to 5th on the third leg, and we then ran Jack Braughton in an endeavour to overhaul the leaders. Jack ran a fine lap in 14.7 which was only 5 seconds outside the course record set up by C.
Walker did our fastest time and only just failed by 1 second to gain an award given for the three fastest laps, which all went to members of the home club.
By the top of Copse Hill Herbert had moved right through the field and four others, Walker, Smart, Short and Tooby went down the hill together.
Cliff Roffey came through for second, Short 3rd., Walker 5th and then the pack Bagnall, Gebbett, Burr, Brickwood and Trower 7th to 11th to make sure of the team race.
Bagnall and Walker ran well for 2nd and 3rd place, followed by the usual crowd with Masters having an easy run whipping up the end of our pack.
Despite a well marked course, Barratt and Cliff Roffey went off course round by the Ponds and eventually Walker and Barratt ran in together.
Walker running in plimsols and a bad cold, did very well to come fifth and with twelve in the first twenty three, we managed to win the team race.

After the first half mile we had Masters, Walker and Bagnall in the first 20, with Patterson Baulch, Short, Trower and Bedford in the twenties, and although positions changed a bit, our scoring six were always placed well in the first thirty.

Burr gained a place but Bagnall was passed by Ken Norris, T.V.H. who did 17.42, the fastest time of the day. Walker gained two places and Roffey put us in the lead. Bedford ran last and was caught by Knight of Essex.
Bedford and Walker then made sure of our victory though Charlie took things a little too easy in the middle and so we missed the course record by one second.

The bulk of our supporters had, by then, assembled on the Common at Mitcham and only Walker and Brown had so far failed to report. The team was not quite as planned as Jumbo Masters still had an injured leg , so Charlie Smart was moved and Eric Gebbett brought into the team.

Jack continued his fine running of this road season and finished only 10 yards behind Reed and in so doing beat the old course record by 15 seconds. Walker then conceded 30 seconds to Peter Pirie and Roffey finishing, had little chance of catching Morgan of S.L.H.
The Junior 100 yards winner also scored a double, Ryan winning from Walker in the short sprint and then in the 220 yards scoring over Key and Walker in 23.5secs.
He was accompanied over the first five miles by Pat Newell, followed by Walker, Bagnall, Short and Gebbett, but at this stage Short retired.

Charlie Walker took the lead quickly, with Baulch, Bagnall and Flanagan on his heels. Round the first lap of the Common, Flanagan went to the front but was not allowed to keep his nose ahead for long.

At the foot of Dale Hill,Charlie Walker waited,as usual, wasting much energy asking all and sundry," what do you think?" Would Charlie pull one out of the bag and put us back in the running for 2nd place?

The field was off to a fast start but it was not until just after the brook that Jack Brown managed to drop Charlie Walker. Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind.
At 5 miles Jack Brown had "lost" the field and looked set for another easy win, Colin Collis followed in 5th position from Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop.
Fortunately S.L.H. and T.V.H. were also in the dumps. 2nd Charlie Walker Conditions perfect for a fast run with twelve teams ahead strung out at regular intervals.

Charlie Walker, however, was spurred on by the responsibility thrown on his shoulders and set out to recover some of the lost ground. By excellent running he passed team after team and the encouraging cheers of the few supporters on this leg kept him at his task.
This year's race,held on a cold damp day, ran true to form with Charlie Walker, who always performs so well over our own courses, the winner by the comfortable margin of 47 seconds.
Toward the end of the first of the three laps Eric Gebbett was our first scorer way back in 49th place followed closely by Charlie Walker 55th.

On entering Cambridge Road with the hills still to come this group had been reduced to Gebbett, Walker, Baulch, Robinson and Shippen. Charlie Walker took over five seconds down on the Valley man and in the course of chasing and catching his quarry he passed three others to give 'Jumbo' Masters the baton, in fifth spot.
In a bunch close behind were Gebbett, Masters, Walker and Robinson with Rogers and Simmons of Mitcham. With two miles to go the leaders, together with 'ghost' A.
Our first team,made up of Shippen, Black, Walker, Robinson, Stearman and Moore wandered between thirteenth and ninth before settling in tenth place- a position far below their capabilities.
Ken Miller was a good third, with Thresher 7th, Walker 8th and Shippen 10th. The home teams were close winners from ourselves with S.L.H. third.

Walker set off on the last stage, in the company of Sale and Milner, to gain third place, but was well below his best and not only did he have to give way to his two opponents but Chelmsford (Hill - Cottingham) and Ponders End (McIntyre) rubbed it in by passing him in the last half-mile.
He finished 7th in 9:09.0, but Bill Kerr had to retire after 5 laps with a troublesome injury and Robinson and Walker were nowhere near their best.
